title: lab 103 - 2026
description: AWS IAM Users, Groups, and Policies

lab_objective.description: In this lab, you will learn how to create IAM users, groups, assign permissions, and implement the Principle of Least Privilege.
lab_objective.scenario: Your company has hired three new employees. As the AWS Administrator, your task is to create the required users, groups, and permissions.
employees: john - LinuxAdmin - Linux Team - EC2 Administrator
sarah - StorageAdmin - Storage Team - S3 Administrator
david - Auditor - Audit Team - S3 Read-only Auditor
objectives: Follow the Principle of Least Privilege

tasks.title: Login to AWS Console
steps: Login to AWS Console using the Root account.

tasks.title: Navigate to IAM
steps: Open AWS Console, Navigate to IAM and access Dashboard
Observe Users, Group, Roles and Policies

tasks.title: Create IAM Groups
steps: Verify all groups appear under IAM User Groups

tasks.title: Create IAM Users
steps: Select Provide user access to the AWS Management Console
Enable Require password reset at the next sign-in

tasks.title: Add Users to Groups
steps: Verify each user belongs to the correct group.

tasks.title: Attach AWS Managed Policies
steps: Do not attach policies directly to users. Use groups only.

tasks.title: Verify Permissions of User john
steps: Attempt to Launch an EC2 Instance

tasks.title: Verify Permissions of User sarah
steps: Attempt to Create an S3 Bucket
Attempt to Launch an EC2 Instance

tasks.title: Modify Group Membership I
steps: Remove user john from LinuxAdmins group
Login again and attempt to Launch an EC2 Instance

tasks.title: Modify Group Membership II
steps: Add user john back to LinuxAdmins group
Login again and verify EC2 access has been restored

completion_message: Excellent work! Continue practicing to strengthen your AWS skills.
